sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Based on the above, the servant's pleasure in his work for the master reflects the master's own pleasure, because the servant's self-nullification connects him to the master's essential delight beyond the command.

translations.translation: And based on this, one will understand what was brought above
(section 7)
from the continuation of 5666,
that the fact that the servant strives that the work he does be for the beauty and glory of his master is because he has pleasure in the work, and his pleasure is the pleasure of the master.
For superficially it is not understood,
behold the connection of the servant to the master is to the level of the master that pertains to him
(that he is subjugated to the master),
and how is the pleasure of the master in the beauty and glory of the work, which is not related
(superficially)
to the subjugation and self-nullification of the servant to the master, felt within him?
And one may say the explanation in the analogue
(and from this it also cascades in the parable),
that through the self-nullification of Kabbalas Ol
(as it is from the aspect that the Torah said "and you shall serve" etc.)
is to complete the intention in this that the Holy One, blessed be He, contracted Himself, as it were, to command the human,
for this intention is in the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself, above the matter of the command,
therefore the matter of the pleasure of the Master Himself is also felt within him.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The fifteenth of Shevat, the New Year for Trees, draws down the power for Torah study with pleasure, and through this, all aspects of divine service are also imbued with delight.

translations.translation: And this is
that on the fifteenth of Shevat, the New Year for the Tree,
for the tree alludes to Torah
(as above, section 2),
that on this day, the giving of power is drawn down for the entire year regarding involvement in Torah,
that the study of Torah should be with diligence and persistence,
and that the Torah he learns should be his pleasure and his vitality
(for the tree is the matter of pleasure,
as above, section 6).
And based on the known principle67
that all four New Years are related to each other,
one may say,
that on the New Year for the Tree, the giving of power is drawn down that also all the matters of man's service
(which are drawn down in the first three New Years)
should be out of pleasure,
in the manner explained above in section 9, that through Torah,
even the service of Kabbalas Ol is with pleasure.
And this is that the New Year for the Tree is on the fifteenth, on which is the fullness of the moon,
and not like the first three New Years which are on Rosh Chodesh, when the moon is only a point,
for that the moon is only a point indicates the matter of self-nullification68,
and the pleasure in the service of G-d,
and particularly the pleasure of Torah,
is the matter of completeness.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Through increased effort in action, service, and especially the study of the inner dimension of Torah with pleasure, the New Year for Kings will be brought to ultimate perfection with the true and complete redemption.

translations.translation: And through the increase in our deeds and our service69,
and particularly in involvement with Torah, and in a manner that Torah is the pleasure and vitality of the person involved in Torah,
and all the more so through the involvement
(and dissemination)
of the inner dimension of Torah
[for in Torah itself, the aspect of the pleasure of Torah is the inner dimension of Torah],
also the New Year for Kings will be in ultimate perfection,
that it will be seen in revelation that all of Israel are children of kings70,
and beyond this—kings
(as is explicit in the Tikkunei Zohar71),
and the children of Israel will go out with an upraised arm72,
as befits kings,
through Dovid, the King Moshiach,
and My servant Dovid shall be king over them etc.73,
in the true and complete redemption,
speedily, literally.
